title: Emergent non-Markovianity in time-delayed waveguide QED
abstract: Quantum systems are invariably coupled to a surrounding environment. A common theoretical method to simplify the problem is to trace over the environment under a Markov approximation, which assumes that the environment holds no memory over the timescales that the system evolves under. In interacting many-body systems, it is often not trivial to extract which of the multiple collective timescales are relevant. We consider a time-delayed waveguide QED setup with a single excitation. By fixing the maximum propagation time and increasing the number of emitters, we show that, even for small delay times, collective effects are sufficient to cause non-Markovianity. The impact of memory is intrinsically state-dependent. For superradiant states, the relevant system timescale is the superradiant lifetime while the relevant bath timescale is the end-to-end delay time. For subradiant states, both timescales depend on the structure of the specific state. Our results demonstrate the importance of prudently making Markov approximations in quantum many-body systems, and highlight potential pitfalls to avoid in scaling up quantum devices to large system sizes.
summary: This paper investigates non-Markovian dynamics in a system of emitters coupled to a time-delayed waveguide. By analyzing the collective behavior in the large emitter limit, the authors show that memory effects become dominant, causing deviations from simple exponential decay. The findings emphasize the critical need for careful consideration of relevant timescales when applying the Markov approximation in complex quantum many-body systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the failure of the Markov approximation in open quantum systems, particularly in complex, many-body settings where environmental memory effects are significant.
main_result: Collective effects in time-delayed waveguide QED can induce non-Markovian dynamics, with the dynamics being governed by an emergent parameter $\chi$ that combines system and environmental timescales.
method: The analysis involves deriving and solving delayed differential equations for emitter amplitudes, comparing results against the Markov approximation, and analyzing the system in the large-$N$ limit.
model_or_system: The system is a time-delayed waveguide Quantum Electrodynamics (wQED) setup consisting of $N$ two-level emitters coupled to a one-dimensional waveguide. The dynamics are modeled using delayed differential equations.
key_observables: Total emitter population, emitted intensity, and the finite-time power spectrum of the emitted field.
important_parameters: The emergent parameter $\chi \equiv N\Gamma\ell/v_g$, the superradiant lifetime, and the end-to-end delay time $	au_\ell$.
main_assumptions: The analysis often assumes a phase-matched geometry and focuses on the single-excitation sector, though it explores deviations from these assumptions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of total population and emitted intensity, showing deviations from the Markovian limit at large $N$, and demonstrate the dependence of dynamics on the parameter $\chi$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the physical model, deriving the governing equations, analyzing the breakdown of the Markov approximation through varying $N$, and finally characterizing the emergent non-Markovian dynamics using the collective parameter $\chi$.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete theoretical examples of how memory effects, arising from system geometry and collective coupling, invalidate standard approximations in quantum optics, which is crucial for designing scalable quantum devices.
